text:
In garden’s hush, the wild winds sigh,
Beneath the watchful, leafy sky.
The flowers bloom, a silent vow,
To show the beauty hidden now.

The ancient trees, in stillness stand,
With wisdom etched in every hand
Of rustling leaves that whisper low,
Of seasons’ turn and time’s slow flow.

Here solace finds the weary heart,
In nature’s cycle, never part.
From bud to bloom, from green to brown,
Life’s story wears a gentle crown.

Yet amidst this green and quiet grace,
A creature walks this hallowed space,
With coat of stark and bold design,
A zebra’s stripes, both black and white, shine.
